VERDICT_FORM.LEVEL_RECOVERY: first bar where a setter is PROVEN TRUE with all higher-priority setters PROVEN FALSE
VERDICT_FORM.TRANSITION_RECOVERY: requires bull_dom identifiable AND the prev-state 3/non-3 PARTITION identifiable — strictly weaker than full LEVEL identifiability

HEAD_SEED.consequence: st[0] = 0 UNCONDITIONALLY; bar-0 predicates are NEVER consulted
HEAD_SEED.flip_at_bar0: tz_state_prev = shift(1, fill_value=0) -> flip[0] = (0==3)&(0!=3) = FALSE, deterministic
HEAD_SEED.AMBIGUITY_NOTE: seed value 0 is ALSO the bear_dom setter value, so a head state of 0 is indistinguishable from a genuine bear_dom collapse

PRIORITY_IS_LOAD_BEARING.consequence: the canonical branch ORDER must be reproduced exactly; assuming exclusivity would misassign state on 20,561 of 143,132 bars

FLIP_IDENTITY.derivation: curr==3 arises only from bull_dom firing, or from carrying a prev of 3. On a carry bar curr==p, so flip=(p==3)&(p!=3)=FALSE always. Hence a flip REQUIRES bull_dom.
FLIP_IDENTITY.consequence: identifiability needs only the 3/non-3 PARTITION of the prior state, not the full state

LEVEL_VS_TRANSITION.case_level_valid_transition_init: F3: prev={1,3}, bull_dom TRUE -> state collapses to singleton {3} (LEVEL VALID) but flip is {TRUE,FALSE} (TRANSITION INIT)
LEVEL_VS_TRANSITION.case_level_init_transition_valid: F6a: prev={3}, bar UNOBSERVED -> state branches to all 6 (LEVEL INIT) but flip is VALID FALSE, because p==3 makes a flip impossible regardless
LEVEL_VS_TRANSITION.why_it_matters: neither can be derived from the other; both must be tracked separately

REACHABLE_STATE_ENGINE.enumeration: priority chain; a setter that MAY fire branches BOTH ways
REACHABLE_STATE_ENGINE.flip_computation: on the (prev, curr) PAIR — never from the two sets independently

UNOBSERVED_BAR.FORBIDDEN: coercing an unobserved bar to the carry branch
UNOBSERVED_BAR.measured_result: reachable set becomes {0,1,2,3,4,5} after one unobserved bar — measured, not assumed

PREDICATE_AVAILABILITY_LAYER.principle: predicate UNKNOWN != predicate FALSE; a setter whose dependencies are not identifiable is UNKNOWN and MUST branch

per_setter_binding_depth_from_source.bull_dom: ema50 (50) | ema20 | swHigh=high.shift(1).rolling(10) | rolling(7) | rolling(3) | compute_signals -> MAX 50
per_setter_binding_depth_from_source.bear_dom: ema50 (50) | ema20 | swLow  | rolling(7) | rolling(3) -> MAX 50

PREDICATE_AVAILABILITY_LAYER.EMA_convention: inherited from the frozen EMA validity convention (period p -> first valid age p)
PREDICATE_AVAILABILITY_LAYER.IMPORTANT_CONSEQUENCE: the six setters have DIFFERENT depth floors (7 / 20 / 50). Between ages 7 and 50 the knowledge vector is PARTIALLY known — some setters proven, others UNKNOWN. The engine supports this natively, so no separate contract is needed; but a single scalar 'first valid age' for sig_tz_flip does NOT exist.
